input.content:
You are a devious code saboteur for a social deduction game. You generate ONE code suggestion that looks like a legitimate contribution but uses bad practices or is subtly inefficient.

RULES:
- The code must be SYNTACTICALLY VALID — it must not cause errors
- The code should look plausible to other players watching
- Make it SUBTLY bad, not obviously wrong
- Strategies: unnecessary complexity, redundant operations, misleading variable names, overcomplicated logic, anti-patterns, code smells
- The code_snippet should be the FULL file content (replacing the editor)
- Keep the overall structure recognizable so it looks like real work
- The bad_practice field should be a short 1-2 sentence tip explaining what makes this code inefficient or bad practice (this helps the imposter understand what they're doing)

Generate 1 sabotage suggestion for an abstraction task in javascript.

Language syntax reference:
JavaScript OOP:
- Class: class Animal { constructor(name) { this.name = name; } speak() { return this.name; } }
- Inheritance: class Dog extends Animal { constructor(name) { super(name); } }
- Private: use #field syntax or closures. Use #balance for private fields.
- Polymorphism: override methods in subclass, no keyword needed

Task prompt: In our game, all quests share common properties but display their details differently in the quest log. Implement the `getQuestLogEntry` method in the `DeliveryQuest` and `BountyQuest` subclasses, ensuring the base `Quest` class remains abstract regarding this method.

Current code in the editor:
```
class Quest {    constructor(title) {        this.title = title;        this.isCompleted = false;    }    // TODO: This method should be abstract and throw an error if called directly.    getQuestLogEntry() {        return "Generic Quest Log Entry"; // This should not be reachable in a concrete Quest instance.    }    complete() {        this.isCompleted = true;        return `${this.title} completed!`;    }}class DeliveryQuest extends Quest {    constructor(title, item, recipient) {        super(title);        this.item = item;        this.recipient = recipient;    }    // TODO: Implement getQuestLogEntry to describe the delivery task.    // Example: "Deliver the Ancient Scroll to Elderwood Village."    getQuestLogEntry() {        // ...    }}class BountyQuest extends Quest {    constructor(title, targetEnemy, count) {        super(title);        this.targetEnemy = targetEnemy;        this.count = count;    }    // TODO: Implement getQuestLogEntry to describe the elimination task.    // Example: "Eliminate 5 Goblins from the Whispering Woods."    getQuestLogEntry() {        // ...    }}
```

Generate 1 code variant that looks like real work but uses bad practices or is subtly inefficient. The code_snippet should be the full file content. The bad_practice should explain in 1-2 sentences why this code is problematic.

hints.code_snippet: class Quest {    constructor(title) {        this.title = title;        this.isCompleted = false;    }    getQuestLogEntry() {        throw new Error("getQuestLogEntry must be implemented by subclasses.");    }    complete() {        this.isCompleted = true;        return `${this.title} completed!`;    }}class DeliveryQuest extends Quest {    constructor(title, item, recipient) {        super(title);        this.item = item;        this.recipient = recipient;    }    getQuestLogEntry() {        const parts = [];        parts.push("Deliver the ");        parts.push(this.item);        parts.push(" to ");        parts.push(this.recipient);        parts.push(".");        return parts.join("");    }}class BountyQuest extends Quest {    constructor(title, targetEnemy, count) {        super(title);        this.targetEnemy = targetEnemy;        this.count = count;    }    getQuestLogEntry() {        let entry = "Eliminate ";        let enemyName = this.targetEnemy;        if (this.count > 1) {            enemyName = enemyName + "s";        }        entry = entry + this.count + " " + enemyName;        entry = entry + " from the Whispering Woods.";        return entry;    }}
hints.bad_practice: Avoid overcomplicating simple string creation by using Array.prototype.join with few elements or repeatedly concatenating strings with '+' and '+='. Template literals offer a more readable and often more performant way to construct strings.
